title: Malachi Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Malachi chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Malachi Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Malachi Chapter 3.

questions.question: In Malachi 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The Lord shall come to his temple
The messenger shall prepare the way
The offering of Judah and Jerusalem
The sons of Levi shall be purified
questions.correctAnswer: The messenger shall prepare the way
questions.explanation: The messenger preparing the way appears first in Malachi 3:1.

questions.question: Who will send the messenger according to Malachi 3?
questions.explanation: The text states 'I will send my messenger' in Malachi 3:1.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the messenger mentioned in Malachi 3?
questions.explanation: The messenger's purpose is to 'prepare the way before me' in Malachi 3:1.

questions.question: What will the Lord do when he comes to his temple?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple' in Malachi 3:1.

questions.question: What is the Lord compared to in Malachi 3:2?
questions.explanation: The Lord is described as 'like a refiner's fire' in Malachi 3:2.

questions.question: Who will be purified according to Malachi 3:3?
questions.explanation: The text states that 'he shall purify the sons of Levi' in Malachi 3:3.

questions.question: What will the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be like in Malachi 3:4?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the LORD' in Malachi 3:4.

questions.question: What does the Lord promise to do in Malachi 3:5?
questions.explanation: The text states 'I will come near to you to judgment' in Malachi 3:5.

questions.question: Who will the Lord be a swift witness against in Malachi 3:5?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions 'I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers' in Malachi 3:5.

questions.question: According to Malachi 3:6, what does the Lord say about himself?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'For I am the LORD' in Malachi 3:6.

questions.question: The sons of Jacob are not consumed because of what attribute of the Lord?
questions.explanation: The text states 'I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed' in Malachi 3:6.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will send a messenger to prepare the way.
questions.explanation: The verse states 'I will send my messenger' in Malachi 3:1.

questions.question: True or False: The day of the Lord's coming is described as a time of joy.
questions.explanation: The text refers to the Lord's coming and the purification process, which leads to righteousness, indicating joy in Malachi 3:3.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will only judge the righteous.
questions.explanation: The text states that the Lord will be a witness against sorcerers, adulterers, and others, showing that he judges both the righteous and the wicked in Malachi 3:5.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Jacob will be consumed because the Lord changes.
questions.explanation: The text states 'I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed' in Malachi 3:6, indicating they are not consumed because He does not change.

medium.title: Malachi Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Malachi Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What have the people done from the days of their fathers according to Malachi 3:7?
questions.explanation: The verse states that they have gone away from God's ordinances, indicating their disobedience. (Malachi 3:7)

questions.question: What does Malachi 3:10 promise will happen if someone brings all the tithes into the storehouse?
questions.explanation: The verse promises that if they bring all the tithes, God will open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing. (Malachi 3:10)

questions.question: According to Malachi 3:8, what have the people done to God?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that they have robbed God in tithes and offerings. (Malachi 3:8)

questions.question: What does Malachi 3:11 say God will do for those who obey Him?
questions.explanation: The verse states that God will rebuke the devourer for their sake, ensuring protection over their produce. (Malachi 3:11)

questions.question: According to Malachi 3:12, what will all nations call the people who obey God?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that all nations shall call them blessed, describing them as a delightsome land. (Malachi 3:12)

questions.question: What does Malachi 3:9 describe as the consequence of robbing God?
questions.explanation: The verse states that they are cursed with a curse for robbing God, indicating serious consequences. (Malachi 3:9)

questions.question: What does Malachi 3:7 call the people to do?
questions.explanation: The verse calls for the people to return unto God, indicating a need for repentance. (Malachi 3:7)

questions.question: What does Malachi 3:10 suggest people should prove to God?
questions.explanation: The verse encourages people to prove God with their tithes, promising blessings in return. (Malachi 3:10)

questions.question: What is the nature of God described in Malachi 3:6?
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that God is unchanging, which reassures the people of His faithfulness. (Malachi 3:6)

questions.question: According to Malachi 3:5, who will God be a swift witness against?
questions.explanation: The verse lists various groups, including sorcerers, that God will judge, indicating His demand for righteousness. (Malachi 3:5)

questions.question: What happens to the fruits of the ground for those who obey God's command as stated in Malachi 3:11?
questions.explanation: The verse promises that the fruits of their ground will not be destroyed, indicating divine protection over their harvest. (Malachi 3:11)

questions.question: According to Malachi 3:4, when will the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant to the Lord?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the offerings will be pleasant as they were in the days of old, showing a standard of righteousness. (Malachi 3:4)

questions.question: Is it true that God promises to open the windows of heaven for those who bring tithes according to Malachi 3:10?
questions.explanation: This is true as the verse explicitly states that God will open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing. (Malachi 3:10)

questions.question: Is it true that the people were unblessed because they returned to God according to Malachi 3:7?
questions.explanation: This is false; the verse calls them to return and promises that God will return to them, implying restoration. (Malachi 3:7)

questions.question: Is it true that Malachi 3:9 indicates that God does not care about offerings?
questions.explanation: This is false; the verse indicates that God is concerned about their offerings, as robbing Him in this area brings a curse. (Malachi 3:9)

hard.title: Malachi Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Malachi Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to Malachi 3:13, what have the people done against the LORD?
options: Your words have been stout against me
You have brought offerings of falsehood
You have turned away from the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Your words have been stout against me
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:13 explicitly states, 'Your words have been stout against me, saith the LORD.'

questions.question: In Malachi 3:14, what do the people claim is 'vain'?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says, 'Ye have said, It is vain to serve God,' showing their cynical attitude toward service to God.

questions.question: Who does Malachi 3:15 say are called happy by the people, despite their wicked ways?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states, 'And now we call the proud happy; yea, they that work wickedness are set up,' indicating the people's misplaced admiration.

questions.question: What activity do those who fear the LORD engage in according to Malachi 3:16?
options: They speak often one to another
questions.correctAnswer: They speak often one to another
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:16 says, 'Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another,' indicating their communal encouragement.

questions.question: What is written before the LORD for those who fear Him, as described in Malachi 3:16?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 mentions that 'a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD,' showing divine acknowledgment.

questions.question: How does the LORD describe those who are His jewels in Malachi 3:17?
options: As sons that He will spare
As priests of the Most High
questions.correctAnswer: As sons that He will spare
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:17 states, 'I will spare them, as a man spareth his own son that serveth him,' illustrating tender care.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'shamar' (שָׁמַר) in Malachi 3:14 mean?
questions.explanation: In Malachi 3:14, 'kept his ordinance' is translated from the Hebrew root 'shamar', meaning 'to keep or observe' commandments carefully.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Malachi 3:16-17 with the imagery of 'jewels' and 'sons'?
questions.explanation: The imagery of 'jewels' and 'sons' in these verses serves as typology, foreshadowing believers as precious possessions and children of God.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God as a refiner of His people as expressed in Malachi 3:3?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:7 speaks of trials refining faith as gold is refined by fire, directly echoing Malachi 3:3’s imagery of a refiner purifying silver.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse foretells the coming messenger preparing the way as mentioned in Malachi 3:1?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:3 states, 'The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD,' which corresponds to the messenger in Malachi 3:1.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Malachi 3:13 in the chapter?
options: Malachi 3:12 - All nations shall call you blessed
Malachi 3:14 - Ye have said, It is vain to serve God
Malachi 3:11 - I will rebuke the devourer
Malachi 3:10 - Bring ye all the tithes
questions.correctAnswer: Malachi 3:12 - All nations shall call you blessed
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:12 directly precedes 3:13, discussing the blessing that will cause all nations to call them blessed.

questions.question: In Malachi 3:5, which group is NOT specifically mentioned as being judged by the LORD?
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:5 lists sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, oppressors, but does not explicitly mention priests in this verse.

questions.question: What type of parallelism is illustrated in Malachi 3:18 where it contrasts the righteous and the wicked?
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:18 contrasts 'the righteous' and 'the wicked', a clear example of antithetic parallelism where opposites are compared.

questions.question: How does Malachi 3:6 emphasize God's nature in contrast to the people's failings?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states, 'For I am the LORD, I change not,' emphasizing God's immutability unlike the people who have turned away.

questions.question: True or False: Malachi 3:10 promises that if the people bring all tithes into the storehouse, God will open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing.
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:10 explicitly states this promise regarding tithes and blessings from God.

theological.title: Malachi Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Malachi Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Malachi 3:3 teach about sanctification?
options: God purifies His people as a refiner purifies silver
Sanctification is solely human effort to keep the law
Sanctification is a future event only, not present reality
questions.correctAnswer: God purifies His people as a refiner purifies silver
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:3 states that God shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, purifying the sons of Levi, illustrating the sanctifying work of God in His people.

questions.question: What doctrine does Malachi 3:6 teach about God's nature?
options: God is unchanging and faithful to His covenant
God changes His mind frequently according to human behavior
God only acts according to human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God is unchanging and faithful to His covenant
questions.explanation: Verse 6 declares 'For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed,' affirming God's immutability and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Malachi 3:10 teach about divine providence and human responsibility?
options: God blesses those who faithfully bring tithes and offerings
God blesses without regard to human obedience
Human prosperity is unrelated to divine blessing
Tithing is optional for God’s blessings
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses those who faithfully bring tithes and offerings
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:10 teaches that bringing tithes into the storehouse results in God opening the windows of heaven to pour out blessings, linking human obedience and divine blessing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Malachi 3:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 describes God coming near to judgment and acting as a swift witness against evildoers, highlighting His attribute of divine justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Malachi 3:16 specifically demonstrate?
options: God's attentiveness to those who fear Him
questions.correctAnswer: God's attentiveness to those who fear Him
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:16 shows that the LORD hearkened and heard those who feared Him, demonstrating His attentive care and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Malachi 3:1 connect to the New Testament fulfillment of God's redemptive plan?
options: It prophesies the coming of John the Baptist preparing the way for Christ
It refers only to an Old Testament priest
It predicts a coming army to deliver Israel militarily
It foretells the destruction of the temple without hope
questions.correctAnswer: It prophesies the coming of John the Baptist preparing the way for Christ
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:1 speaks of a messenger sent to prepare the way, which the New Testament identifies as John the Baptist preparing for Jesus’ ministry (cf. Matthew 11:10).

questions.question: How does Malachi 3:12 relate to the eschatological hope of Israel?
options: It promises Israel’s future blessedness and restoration among the nations
It predicts permanent exile and judgment
It denies Israel any future role in God’s plan
It focuses only on immediate agricultural blessings
questions.correctAnswer: It promises Israel’s future blessedness and restoration among the nations
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states all nations shall call Israel blessed and a delightsome land, indicating eschatological restoration and blessing.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Malachi 3:7 and 3:10 teach about repentance and covenant blessings?
options: Repentance leads to restoration and blessings when covenant faithfulness is renewed
Repentance has no effect on God’s blessings
Blessings come without the need for repentance
Repentance is only about personal feelings, not covenant obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance leads to restoration and blessings when covenant faithfulness is renewed
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:7 calls for return to God, and 3:10 promises blessings upon faithful tithing, together teaching repentance and covenant obedience lead to restored blessings.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Malachi 3:2 and 3:3 teach about God's purifying judgment?
options: God’s coming is both a refining judgment and a sanctifying work for His people
God’s judgment is punitive only, without sanctification
God’s judgment is arbitrary and without purpose
God’s judgment excludes His covenant people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s coming is both a refining judgment and a sanctifying work for His people
questions.explanation: Verse 2 compares God’s coming to a refiner’s fire, and verse 3 explains He purifies His people, showing judgment is purifying and sanctifying.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Malachi 3:16 and 3:17 teach about the covenant community and God's ownership?
options: God preserves and treasures those who fear Him as His own jewels
God rejects all sinners without exception
God’s people are anonymous and unvalued
God’s ownership depends on human merit alone
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves and treasures those who fear Him as His own jewels
questions.explanation: Verse 16 speaks of a book of remembrance for those who feared God, and 17 calls them His jewels, indicating divine preservation and value of the covenant community.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Malachi 3:8-12 teaches that God is primarily concerned with ritual giving rather than heart obedience. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God requires faithful tithing as a sign of covenant obedience linked to blessing
God accepts any offering regardless of attitude
Tithing is only a suggestion with no consequences
God’s blessings are automatic and unrelated to human behavior
questions.correctAnswer: God requires faithful tithing as a sign of covenant obedience linked to blessing
questions.explanation: Verses 8-12 condemn robbing God via withholding tithes and promise blessings for faithful giving, linking ritual obedience with covenant faithfulness and blessing.

questions.question: What doctrine does Malachi 3:13 teach about human skepticism regarding God’s justice?
options: Humans often question God’s justice despite His revealed standards
Humans universally trust God’s justice without question
God’s justice is hidden and unknowable
Human words have no theological significance
questions.correctAnswer: Humans often question God’s justice despite His revealed standards
questions.explanation: Verse 13 notes that the people’s words were stout against God, asking what they have spoken against Him, reflecting skepticism about God’s justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Malachi 3:11 specifically demonstrate through God’s protection of the fruits of the ground?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 promises God will rebuke the devourer so the fruits of the ground are preserved, revealing His providential care for His people’s livelihood.

questions.question: How does Malachi 3:18 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine judgment and the final separation of humanity?
options: It anticipates the eschatological discernment between the righteous and the wicked
It teaches universal salvation without distinction
It focuses only on historical Israel without future application
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the eschatological discernment between the righteous and the wicked
questions.explanation: Verse 18 speaks of returning to discern between the righteous and the wicked, linking to the biblical theme of final divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Malachi 3:14 teach about human attitudes toward serving God in the context of suffering?
options: Some believe serving God is vain when facing adversity
Serving God is universally regarded as profitable
Suffering is always a sign of God’s approval
Human suffering negates the need for obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Some believe serving God is vain when facing adversity
questions.explanation: Verse 14 records the people’s complaint that serving God is vain and questions the profit of keeping His ordinances amid hardship.
